reviewFindings.title: Preserve the cancellation signal when draining queued tasks
reviewFindings.body: Queued requests are the default, but `drain()` passes `execute({ input: task.input }, transport)`, discarding the signal newly stored by `submit()`. An already-aborted queued request therefore still invokes transport, and an active queued request's transport never receives its signal. The queue itself preserves the task, so pass that complete task to `execute()` to make both documented cancellation behaviors work.

result.solutionAssessment: No, not as submitted: the shared-worker approach is appropriately narrow, but only immediate requests reach it with their signal intact. Forwarding the original queued task completes the design without another cancellation implementation.
